title: PrepKit Inventory Export
description: The user's actual holdings: what a running instance stores and what a full export contains. Distinct from kit-template.schema.json, which describes an aspirational standard. The central modelling decision here is the Item/Lot split: an Item is a type of thing you own ('canned chili'), a Lot is a dated batch of it ('6 cans, best-by 2027-03'). Expiration lives on Lots. Collapsing the two makes partial rotation unrepresentable and is the most common way inventory tools get this wrong.

instance_id.description: Stable per-installation identifier. Needed later for multi-device sync conflict attribution; harmless now.

household.description: Drives per_person and per_person_per_day scaling. Deliberately minimal: this is planning input, not a personnel file.

label.description: How the household refers to them. A role ('parent 1', 'youngest') is sufficient and preferred over a full legal name for anything that may be exported to a device that leaves the house.

age_band.description: Age band rather than birthdate: enough for consumable scaling and kit sizing, without carrying a precise identifier into exports.

needs.description: Free-text planning notes that affect what the household must stock (dietary restriction, mobility aid, prescription dependency). Treated as SENSITIVE: consumers MUST exclude this field from any unencrypted export by default, and MUST require explicit opt-in per export.

container.description: Nestable physical vessel. A pouch inside a pack inside a vehicle is three containers, two edges. Self-referential parentage MUST be rejected on write.

color_code.description: Physical color-coding of the vessel, if the user follows a color convention. Free-form: it records the real pouch's color, which may or may not match a category's canonical color.

qr_slug.description: Short opaque token printed on the container's label. MUST NOT encode a URL containing personal data, and MUST be resolvable only against the local instance.

weight_g.description: Empty weight of the vessel itself.

kit.description: A user's real instance of a preparedness kit, optionally scored against a template.

template_id.description: Slug of the template this was instantiated from, if any. Retained after instantiation so the kit can be re-scored when the template is updated.

last_verified.description: Last time a human physically opened this kit and confirmed contents. Distinct from any record edit timestamp: a database that has drifted from the actual bag is the failure this field exists to expose.

item.description: A type of thing the user owns. Non-expiring items carry their quantity here directly; expiring items leave quantity null and carry it on their Lots.

template_item_id.description: Which template line this satisfies. This is what lets a user's chosen product count toward a generic requirement, and what makes substitution survive a template upgrade.

quantity.description: Present for non-consumables. MUST be null or absent when the item has lots; deriving it from the sum of lot quantities prevents the two from disagreeing.

product.description: The actual make and model the user owns. Free-form and user-supplied. Unlike a template exemplar this carries no recommendation.

cost.description: Optional. Useful for insurance documentation. Treated as SENSITIVE for export purposes.

serial.description: SENSITIVE. Valuable for insurance claims and theft recovery, and for exactly that reason MUST be excluded from unencrypted exports by default.

lot.description: A dated batch of a consumable item. Multiple lots per item is the normal case, not an edge case: it is how partial rotation is represented.

expires.description: The printed date, transcribed as-is. Absent for items that degrade without a printed date; those rely on next_check instead.

expiry_basis.description: What the date means. 'Best by' on rice and 'use by' on infant formula are different in kind, and a rotation dashboard that treats them identically gives bad advice. Consumers SHOULD distinguish them in reporting.

opened.description: Once opened, printed shelf life usually no longer applies.

next_check.description: Next physical inspection due. The primary mechanism for items with no printed date (stored fuel, batteries, seals) and a secondary one for everything else.

container_id.description: Lots of one item may sit in different places. Overrides the parent item's container when present.

document.description: Critical information. SENSITIVE BY DEFAULT: every field here is assumed confidential, and this entity MUST NOT appear in any unencrypted export unless the user explicitly opts in per export. See docs/threat-model.md before implementing storage.

body.description: Markdown content, for documents authored in-app such as a communications plan or rendezvous list.

review_interval_months.description: Plans decay. A rendezvous point at a since-demolished building is worse than none, so plans get review reminders exactly as consumables get expiry reminders.

export_ok.description: Explicit per-document opt-in for inclusion in offline exports. Defaults false. Consumers MUST NOT provide a blanket 'export everything' switch that bypasses this.

maintenance_event.description: Log of physical actions taken. The audit trail that distinguishes a kit genuinely verified last month from one whose record merely says so.
